title: Cacio e Pepe
description: Rome's three-ingredient pasta: cracked black pepper bloomed in a dry pan, then emulsified with Pecorino Romano and starchy pasta water until it turns glossy, not clumpy.

image.alt: Bowtie pasta with black pepper and pecorino in a dark ceramic bowl, moody light

ingredients: 1 tsp whole black peppercorns, coarsely cracked
100g Pecorino Romano, finely grated, plus extra to serve
Fine sea salt, for the pasta water
steps: Bring a pot of water to a boil and salt it lightly — go easy, since Pecorino brings plenty of salt on its own.
Toast the cracked peppercorns in a dry skillet over medium heat for 1–2 minutes until fragrant, then add a ladle of pasta water and simmer gently to infuse.
Cook the pasta 2 minutes short of the package time. Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.
Off the heat, add the pasta to the skillet with a splash more pasta water.
Add the Pecorino a handful at a time, tossing constantly and adding pasta water as needed, until the sauce clings in a glossy emulsion with no dry clumps and no soupy pool.
Plate immediately with extra cracked pepper and Pecorino.
note: Take the skillet off the heat before adding cheese — Pecorino seizes into strings above about 70°C.
